The Bellman optimality equation

The Bellman expectation equation averages over the actions a policy might take. The optimal values satisfy the same equation with that average replaced by a max: from every state, take the best action, then keep behaving optimally. That single change makes the equation non-linear.

Backup:

average of the $q$s
max of the $q$s

Why max breaks the matrix trick

One state, two actions. "Stay" pays 1 and comes back to the same state. "Leave" pays $L$ and ends the episode. The optimal value solves $v = \max(1 + \gamma v,\; L)$. Plot both sides: the solution is where the kinked green line meets the grey diagonal (amber line).

The maths

From Lesson 24, an optimal agent takes the best action, so $v_*(s) = \max_a q_*(s, a)$. After that first action it behaves optimally, so the action value is one step of reward plus the optimal value of wherever it lands:

$$q_*(s, a) = \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\,\big[r + \gamma\, v_*(s')\big]$$

Put the two together to get the Bellman optimality equation for $v_*$:

$$v_*(s) = \max_a \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\,\big[r + \gamma\, v_*(s')\big]$$

Compare Lesson 26: the only change is $\sum_a \pi(a \mid s)$ becoming $\max_a$. In the backup diagram the average over action branches becomes an arc that picks the best branch. The same substitution gives the version for action values:

$$q_*(s, a) = \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\Big[r + \gamma \max_{a'} q_*(s', a')\Big]$$

The optimality equation makes no mention of any policy. For a finite MDP with $\gamma < 1$ it has exactly one solution, $v_*$. Once $v_*$ is known, any policy that is greedy with respect to its one-step lookahead is optimal. The small arrows on the grid are that policy.

The catch: $\max$ is not linear, so there is no $(I - \gamma P)^{-1}$ to compute. In the plot, the right-hand side has a kink, and which piece you are on depends on the answer. With $\gamma = 0.9$ and $L = 5$, staying forever is worth $1/(1 - 0.9) = 10 > 5$, so $v_* = 10$. Large MDPs are solved by iteration instead: value iteration (Lesson 33) applies the max backup again and again.
